newsitem.title: USA: Fed seen out of open market until Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Fed seen out of open market until Tuesday.

text.p: The Federal Reserve is expected to stay on the sidelines Friday, as the day's add requirement was said to have been met with Thursday's operation, analysts said.

The Fed added reserves to the banking system via a round of five-day fixed system repurchase agreements Thursday. Analysts said those RPs should be sufficient to take care of the add need through the Veterans holiday on Monday, when the Fed is closed. But, analysts said, the Fed will need to add reserves again Tuesday.

The add need is seen around $6.5 billion a day for the current maintenance period, which began Thursday. Part of the add need was taken care of when the Fed bought bills Wednesday for Thursday delivery -- a bill pass. Analysts predict the bill pass was about $4 billion.
